sampling: 12 records matching the representative set published in FINDINGS, plus 10 drawn from the remaining 41 by a fixed FNV-1a hash of seed-20260805 + the record text, so the draw is reproducible
method: Each recorded correction was split into its two competing statements, verdict words removed, order shuffled by idx parity so the adjudicator could not tell which was original. Adjudicators read source only, were told to default to CANNOT_DETERMINE, and to state how the rejected statement could still be defensible.
limitations: Blinding was partial. The corrected half of each pair is systematically more detailed, because it was written after reading source, so an adjudicator could plausibly infer which was which from specificity alone. That heuristic correlates with truth, so it cannot be separated from the verdict here. Each adjudicator did supply independent source evidence, which mitigates but does not remove the leak.

Zero CANNOT_DETERMINE verdicts across 22, all at high confidence, despite an explicit instruction to abstain when the source does not settle the question. That is the profile of either a genuinely clear-cut sample or an instrument that is not discriminating. The quoted evidence — exact line numbers, grep output, runtime stdout — argues for the former, and the notes do actively defend the losing statement, but a 22/22 high-confidence sweep should be read with that in mind.
n = 22 of 53. Extrapolating 21/22 to the population gives a wide interval; the defensible statement is that most corrections hold and none of the sampled ones was overturned.
